messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Sally Chen <sally@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft scores and narrative for final adjudication

Team —

Attached is the evidence pack and my proposed final scores for the OKR set for Q1. I ran the grade sheet against the rubric we agreed on (clarity, measurable outcomes, customer impact, and effort-to-value). Highlights and asks below:

- Objective A (Improve serving latency): proposed 4/5. Evidence: latency histograms, 95th percentile under target for 72% of windows. See sheet row 3.
- Objective B (Reduce unit cost by 25% on analytics workload): proposed 3/5. We hit ~18% at quarter close; caching improvements landed late.
- Objective C (Customer adoption & pilot expansion — Acme): proposed 2/5. Pilot active but migration stalled; Sally is cc'd for final adoption notes.

Open questions: Karthik flagged accuracy of the cost attribution (cloud vs infra) — I included the cost breakdown in the spreadsheet but we should agree on a single number for publication. Rishi, can you confirm the final finance-adjusted number by EOD Thursday?

If there are no further objections, I propose we publish the scores and the narrative packet on Monday morning for the QBR prep. If anyone expects to raise a formal dispute, please reply and summarize the evidence you want considered.

Attachments: okr-evidence-pack-Mar31.pdf, okr-score-rationales.xlsx

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the packet, very thorough. Two quick items:

2) For Objective C (Acme), Sally — short ask: can you confirm the list of production feature gates you still need us to clear? We want the narrative to reflect the exact blocker.

Otherwise, +1 to publishing once we reconcile the cost number.

Quick objection and request for clarification on Objective B cost numbers.

I raised this earlier in the working doc: the cost reduction figure in the evidence pack mixes amortized infra (reserved capacity) savings with host-level batching improvements. For the QBR we should report the customer-visible unit cost (what they actually pay-per-request) and then annotate the internal split as a secondary line item. The current wording implies all savings are customer-facing, which overstates our delivery to customers.

Ask: Marissa / Rishi — can we create a one-line table that shows (a) customer-visible unit cost change, (b) internal efficiency delta, and (c) one-sentence rationale? I can draft the table if you want — prefer to include it in the narrative before publishing.

Karthik
Senior Manager, Platform Performance
Redwood Inference

Team —

Thanks for the fast turns. Summary of decisions and next steps (actionable items only):

1) Final scores (published): A 4/5, B 3/5, C 2/5. Narrative updated with Vivek's two leadership learnings and Laura's note about traffic shape.
2) Cost reporting: we'll publish the customer-visible unit cost (17.9%) as the headline and include the finance-adjusted internal split (+4.1%) as an annotated footnote in the narrative. Karthik's requested one-line table included (see updated xlsx).
3) Acme adoption blockers: Sally confirmed feature gates needed (feature-flag doc link inside Drive file). We documented the blocker language exactly as requested by the customer.
4) Publication: Marissa will push the narrative and the evidence pack to the QBR folder on Monday 08:00 PST and notify the execs. Vivek will have the talking track bullet points ready by Monday 10:00 PST.

If no objections by EOD Monday I'll proceed with publication and request DocuSign for the small credits memo we agreed to for Acme (DocuSign link below).
